changes.title: F-11: a design had no moderator result
changes.problem: In a design run the moderator checked the design and had the designer fix it once, but wrote nothing down. proposal.json held only the designer's part, so neither the results nor the UX suite showed the moderator's word on a design. A round does have it, in round.json.
changes.fix: The proposal prompt names the moderator and has it write check.json (verdict ready / ready-with-remarks / not-ready, summary, found with fixed or not, remaining) before the run may say done. versions() carries it as `check`, and the Designs tab shows it under the design, or says that a finished design has none.

changes.title: F-10: the framework named no place for the product, and nothing put a project back in place
changes.problem: CRISSP.md only said 'the root keeps the product'. The template's steps pointed at src/ with no `when`, its UX suite walked a Vite dev server (127.0.0.1:5173), and deploy.json expected app/backend and app/frontend. So a first session hand-built a prototype inside crissp/uxsuite/ and served it as the product. The template's agreement also named a crissp/tool an installed project does not have.
changes.fix: D-02: app/backend + app/frontend + docker-compose.yml is the default (CRISSP.md 'The product's place', the template's agreement). The template's steps (backend, backend-lint, frontend) exist once their part does, and the UX suite walks the Compose stack (8080). crissp repair (lib/repair.py) shows what a project has out of place: old steps, the old UX address, files in crissp/uxsuite/, the old agreement line, missing template files, an old CRISSP.md, missing ignore rules. crissp repair --yes puts each in place; it never deletes, never commits and never changes the backlog's content.

changes.title: F-09: crissp dashboard opened another project's dashboard
changes.problem: test.sh reused any crissp dashboard answering on the port without checking which project it served: with one project's dashboard running, crissp dashboard in a second project opened the first, so the second's tests and UX results seemed missing. The crissp tool's dashboard action had the same check.
changes.fix: The stamp (/dashboard/stamp) names the project it serves; lib/place.py picks the port: this project's dashboard is reused, another project's (or one that does not say whose) is left alone and the next free port taken with a note, a program that is no dashboard on the asked port stops it with a clear message. The tool's served() also requires the stamp to name its project.

changes.title: F-08: every green full run asked for a commit that only recorded a hash
changes.problem: The gate rewrote coverage-baseline.json on every green run of every suite, with only a new commit hash when no number changed, so every full run ended with 'the coverage baseline went up: commit …'.
changes.fix: lib/gate.py writes the baseline only when something moves: no baseline yet, --accept, a number that changed, or a commit the diff rule needs (none recorded, or one git no longer knows). Otherwise the older commit stays: the next diff rule looks back further, stricter, never laxer.

changes.title: F-01: crissp refused every option meant for a guard
changes.problem: crissp check --plan, crissp deploy --cluster and crissp ux --shoot <walk> were refused: argparse's REMAINDER does not pass a leading --option on to a subcommand.
changes.fix: src/crissp/cli.py splits the command line at the guard's name and passes the rest to the guard untouched.

changes.title: F-02: approving a design failed in an installed project
changes.problem: The UX suite looked for the crissp tool only inside the project; a project made with crissp init has none, so Approve answered 400.
changes.fix: ux_backlog.tool() uses the project's own crissp/tool, else the engine's; designs show before and after with Approve, Approve with a remark, Again and Reject, and a remark comes first in the PBI.

changes.title: F-03: pytest 9.0.3, and a UX test that read the wrong project
changes.problem: The CVE audit flagged pytest 8.4.2 (PYSEC-2026-1845); a UX test inherited the run's CRISSP_ROOT and read this repository during a full run.
changes.fix: pytest 9.0.3 pinned in crissp/testsuite/requirements.txt; the test starts ux.sh without CRISSP_ROOT.

changes.title: F-04: an installed project's guards named script paths it does not have
changes.problem: In a project made with crissp init the guards said 'crissp/deploy.sh may go', 'run crissp/check-all.sh': files that only exist in a repository that carries the framework.
changes.fix: The crissp command sets CRISSP_COMMAND; project.speak() and the Speaking stream every guard writes through name crissp check, check-all, deploy, dashboard and ux instead; deploy.sh's messages and the UX suite's (and the PBIs it writes) do the same.

changes.title: F-06: the first full run did not say what was left
changes.problem: A new project's first green full run ended with 'the coverage baseline went up: commit …', which a new user could not place.
changes.fix: check.py tells a first baseline (not in git yet) from a raised one, and for the first says plainly: commit it, then crissp check moves the certificate, with the exact commands.

changes.title: check.sh crashed outside a git checkout
changes.problem: The repository was taken out of git to become a project of its own; check.sh then failed on git commands with no clear reason, and check-all.sh refused to prove the tree at all.
changes.fix: lib/check.py (check.sh and check-all.sh are its doors) asks first whether the project is a git checkout: check.sh stops with exit 2 and says to run git init and commit; check-all.sh still runs every step for proof and writes no release certificate.

changes.title: The guards named one product's parts in their code
changes.problem: impact.py, run.sh, the gate, the certificate, setup and the audit named a backend, a frontend and their tools in code, so every other product had to edit the framework itself.
changes.fix: One configuration, crissp/testsuite/suites.json (lib/project.py), describes the product's steps (folder, command, coverage, gate), what a change runs (paths), its shared ground, setup and audit; every guard reads it, and run.py runs the steps.

changes.title: The tools found the project from their own file location
changes.problem: Every library reached the repository's root with Path(__file__).parents[n], so the engine could not live apart from a project's data.
changes.fix: The project is CRISSP_ROOT or the current directory (the scripts export CRISSP_ROOT); only the engine's own files (the dashboard page, the look, the UX page) are found next to the code.

changes.title: The Tests dashboard and the UX suite looked different and ran apart
changes.problem: The dashboard and the UX suite had their own looks, ports and servers, and nothing linked an approved design to the PBI it became.
changes.fix: One local server (lib/serve.py) serves /dashboard/, /ux/ and the shared look in crissp/look (tokens, font, theme, water), and nothing else of the repository; an approved design becomes a PBI through the crissp tool, and the board links it back.

gaps: No browser test of the framework's own pages: the dashboard's and the UX suite's JavaScript (app.js, ux.js, look.js) run only in a person's browser; the tests prove the data and the server behind them.
The UX team's rounds and designs are headless Claude Code runs and its screenshots need Playwright's Chromium: both are stood in by the tests, no real round has been proven by a test.
The deploy step needs helm (and terraform for its fmt and validate) on the machine; without terraform that part is skipped with a visible line, not proven.
The CVE audit needs the network (uv resolves the pinned tools, pip-audit asks the advisories): offline the audit step is red, never green.
Without git there is no release certificate: check.sh stops and check-all.sh proves the tree but certifies nothing until the repository has commits.
The coverage baseline starts empty: the first green full run with a commit sets it, and until then the rule that every changed line is covered is skipped.
